Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Conditionally permitted for a Low_Risk_Standard wholesale distributor of passive electronic components: a commercial virtual-office package providing a genuine Spanish physical address, mail handling, telephone reception, legal-address domiciliation and AEAT notification access may satisfy the registered-office requirement under art. 9 of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), provided the address is not a mere PO Box, the management in fact directs operations from a verifiable location, and the notary and Registro Mercantil find no indicia of sham establishment. For tax substance, the AEAT requires that the place of effective management or a permanent establishment be verifiable in Spain; pure mail-forwarding without administrative or transactional substance is not per se sufficient and may trigger tax-residency or re-domiciliation challenges.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The competent Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the province of the registered office, under the coordination of the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 19-23 (formation and articles), 32-33 (registration and legal personality), 58-62 (capital contributions), 210-242 (administration), and 279-284 (annual accounts filing). Law 14/2013 and subsequent electronic formation rules may permit accelerated online processing. Law 18/2022 reduced the statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to EUR 1 and introduced additional creditor-protection rules while capital remains below EUR 3,000.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) executed before a Spanish notary and filed for registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, together with the certified articles of association and beneficial ownership information.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 47 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

The minimum share capital is EUR 1. All subscribed capital must be fully paid at incorporation. Monetary contributions are normally evidenced by a bank certificate, although the founders may dispense with delivery of the certificate and assume statutory liability for the reality of the contribution under the Companies Act. No statutory escrow account is required; a dedicated pre-incorporation bank account is customary where a bank certificate is used. If capital is below EUR 3,000, the statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules applicable under Law 18/2022 must be observed.

Funding & unlock path: Obtain or document municipal fire-safety compliance under the applicable Building Code, fire-protection rules, and local technical requirements, including emergency exits, extinguishers, fire compartmentation, signage, and emergency lighting. Where applicable, obtain a technical fire report and certificates for electrical and fire-protection installations. Verify structural floor loading and storage-rack safety for warehouse operations. Complete occupational risk assessment, prevention planning, worker training, personal protective equipment controls, emergency procedures, and workplace registration or notification requirements before commencing operations.

Paid-in capital rule: The minimum share capital is EUR 1. All subscribed capital must be fully paid at incorporation. Monetary contributions are normally evidenced by a bank certificate, although the founders may dispense with delivery of the certificate and assume statutory liability for the reality of the contribution under the Companies Act. No statutory escrow account is required; a dedicated pre-incorporation bank account is customary where a bank certificate is used. If capital is below EUR 3,000, the statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules applicable under Law 18/2022 must be observed.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that: (1) the Company accepts and records the subscription and full payment of its share capital by the founding shareholder in accordance with the incorporation deed and articles; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted for all corporate and statutory purposes; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, if applicable, [names] are appointed joint or several directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) the appointed officer is authorized to obtain the tax identification number, complete Commercial Registry filings, open the corporate bank account, and execute all documents necessary to commence the Company’s business.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

The industrial authority of the Autonomous Community in which the premises are located, together with the relevant municipal authority. For ordinary distribution of passive electronic components, no national manufacturing license is ordinarily required; additional regional registration may apply if the premises constitute a regulated industrial establishment or handle regulated equipment or waste.

Category: Municipal activity and opening authorization (licencia de actividad y apertura), or a municipal responsible declaration or prior communication (declaración responsable or comunicación previa), depending on the Autonomous Community, municipality, premises, and activity classification.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), through the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT. The competent tax administration is generally the AEAT; the Basque Country and Navarre have separate foral tax administrations for taxpayers within their respective territorial regimes.

E-government filing portal

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF), generally beginning with the letter B, through the Modelo 036 census registration process. The provisional NIF is normally requested during incorporation through the notarial and commercial-registry one-stop process and must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry. A foreign shareholder or director without a Spanish tax number must generally obtain an individual or foreign-entity NIF as applicable. A non-resident entity carrying on business, holding Spanish tax obligations, or requiring Spanish VAT registration applies for an NIF through Modelo 036, submitting constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, identification of directors or legal representatives, and evidence of authority of the Spanish tax representative where required. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and certified Spanish translation. For intra-EU transactions, the entity separately requests registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036; the resulting Spanish VAT identification number is generally the NIF prefixed with ES and is validated through VIES. The entity must report changes in tax domicile, activities, representatives, VAT status, and census data through the applicable AEAT filing.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada obtains a Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF), generally beginning with the letter B, through the Modelo 036 census registration process. The provisional NIF is normally requested during incorporation through the notarial and commercial-registry one-stop process and must be converted into a definitive NIF after registration with the Commercial Registry. A foreign shareholder or director without a Spanish tax number must generally obtain an individual or foreign-entity NIF as applicable. A non-resident entity carrying on business, holding Spanish tax obligations, or requiring Spanish VAT registration applies for an NIF through Modelo 036, submitting constitutional documents, evidence of legal existence, identification of directors or legal representatives, and evidence of authority of the Spanish tax representative where required. Foreign documents may require apostille or legalization and certified Spanish translation. For intra-EU transactions, the entity separately requests registration in the Registro de Operadores Intracomunitarios through Modelo 036; the resulting Spanish VAT identification number is generally the NIF prefixed with ES and is validated through VIES. The entity must report changes in tax domicile, activities, representatives, VAT status, and census data through the applicable AEAT filing.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

There is no general United States-style check-the-box election for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. The SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person. Available elections or applications may include the consolidated tax regime for qualifying corporate groups, the special regime for mergers, demergers, asset contributions and exchanges, the special regime for entities engaged in leasing residential property where statutory conditions are met, the Canaries tax regimes where geographically applicable, and the VAT special regime for groups of entities. A Spanish tax-transparent or pass-through treatment is not generally available for an SL merely by election. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or neutralize duplicate deductions and imported mismatches under the Spanish implementation of ATAD rules.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover threshold applies for ordinary Spanish VAT registration. A business must generally register before commencing taxable activities, making taxable supplies, acquiring goods or services that create Spanish VAT obligations, or importing goods. The €10,000 EU-wide threshold for certain intra-EU distance sales and qualifying cross-border B2C digital, telecommunications, broadcasting, and electronically supplied services is not a general domestic VAT-registration threshold; eligible businesses may use the Union or Non-Union One Stop Shop where applicable.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods dispatched or transported from mainland Spain or the Balearic Islands to destinations outside the EU VAT territory may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT, provided the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the exporter retains reliable proof that the goods left the EU. Direct exports require dispatch by or on behalf of the Spanish supplier; indirect exports generally require dispatch by or on behalf of a non-EU purchaser and compliance with the applicable passenger or commercial export procedure. Intra-EU supplies of goods may qualify for exemption with the right to deduct input VAT where the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier holds the required evidence and reports the transaction correctly. B2B services are generally located where the business customer is established and may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT rather than technically zero-rated; special rules apply to services connected with immovable property, transport, events, intermediaries, and use and enjoyment. Evidence must be consistent with customs records, commercial invoices, transport documentation, customer VAT data, and required VAT returns or recapitulative statements.

  • Commercial invoice identifying the Spanish supplier, customer, goods, quantities, values, and contractual delivery terms
  • Electronic export declaration submitted through the Spanish customs system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
  • Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic evidence that the goods physically exited the EU customs territory
  • Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, sea waybill, air waybill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or carrier confirmation
  • Packing list and warehouse dispatch or delivery records where relevant
  • Proof of the purchaser's non-EU status or destination, where required by the applicable export procedure
  • Import or customs-clearance evidence in the destination country where available and commercially appropriate
  • VAT accounting records and relevant Modelo 303 and Modelo 349 support
  • Inward remittance or bank-payment evidence where used as corroboration; it is not generally a universal statutory substitute for customs exit evidence

Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for all domestic invoices. The Immediate Supply of Information (SII) system requires qualifying taxpayers, including businesses with turnover exceeding €6 million, members of VAT groups, and entities registered in the monthly VAT refund regime, to transmit invoice-register data electronically to the AEAT generally within four business days, extended to eight business days for invoices issued by the recipient or a third party. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for specified public-sector transactions and is being expanded for private-sector B2B transactions under the Law on the Creation and Growth of Companies, subject to implementing regulations and phased effective dates. Spain's VERI*FACTU and invoicing-system integrity rules require compliant software controls, traceability, preservation, and anti-tampering features; the applicable technical and implementation timetable must be monitored before deployment. Basque Country and Navarre may impose additional regional systems, including TicketBAI or equivalent requirements, where the entity is subject to the relevant foral tax administration.

Spain has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline of 180 days for export proceeds. Export VAT exemption is vulnerable to assessment where the taxpayer cannot prove dispatch, transport, customer status, customs exit, or correct reporting. The AEAT may retrospectively deny the exemption, assess unpaid VAT at the applicable rate, recover improperly refunded or deducted input VAT, and charge late-payment interest. Monetary penalties may apply for incorrect, incomplete, or fraudulent tax returns, failure to issue or retain compliant invoices, obstruction of inspection, and use of false or unreliable evidence; serious or very serious infringements can produce percentage-based penalties linked to the unpaid or improperly refunded tax, with aggravation for concealment, repeated conduct, or fraudulent means. Customs infringements may trigger separate customs debt, interest, fines, and loss of simplified or authorized-economic-operator privileges. Deliberate tax fraud may also create criminal exposure where statutory criminal thresholds and intent requirements are met.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a full Eurozone member; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. No exchange control authorization or central-bank permit is required for an ES_SL to receive export proceeds, inject foreign equity, pay foreign suppliers, remit dividends or repatriate capital. The only binding compliance layers are statistical declarations to Banco de España (Form TE for individual cross-border flows at or above EUR 50,000, filed monthly within the first ten business days), the ex-post registration of foreign direct investment (D-1A form to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month; prior-to-execution filing applies where the investment amount exceeds EUR 3,000,000) and the EU foreign investment screening regime (RD-Law 34/2020), which does not affect ISIC 4652 electronic-components wholesale because it is outside the critical-infrastructure, dual-use or national-security sector list. Profit remittance and dividends face no FX hurdle; the paying Spanish bank may only ask for evidence of tax residence, a solvency certificate and an anti-money-laundering source-of-funds update before executing repeated remittances.

Export proceeds surrender rules

There are no export-proceeds surrender rules and no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR; this was abolished by the 1991 liberalization. An ES_SL may collect and retain export proceeds in any convertible currency, including USD or CNY, in accounts held at Spanish credit institutions or abroad. Reporting obligations apply only for statistical consistency: individual export-collection transactions equal to or greater than EUR 50,000 must be reported via Form TE to Banco de España within the first ten business days of the month following receipt; lower-value goods flows are captured by the customs SAD declarations. There is no time limit within which receivables must be repatriated, provided the company complies with transfer-pricing (Article 16 LIS) and Spanish controlled-foreign-company rules under the General Tax Law (LGT).

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) exercises exchange-control supervision as an Eurosystem NCB, supported by the Secretaría de Estado de Comercio (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa) for the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores and by SEPBLAC (Spanish AML/FIU) for banking onboarding oversight. The legal liberalization framework is EU Art. 63 TFEU, Royal Decree 1816/1991 (operaciones de pago con el exterior), RD 571/2023 (foreign investment registry) and Ley 10/2010/RD 304/2014 for AML-KYC.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Conditional — rated Low as a sole treasury spine and Medium as a supplementary settlement overlay. Spanish-licensed or passported EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) operating under PSD2 and supervised by Banco de España can open transactional EUR/GBP/USD accounts for an ES_SL without a physical branch visit, with e-KYC under RD 304/2014, and can provide cheaper MT103-correspondent-grade payments and FX conversion for the passive-components distribution flows. Legal constraints are material: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot issue commercial documentary letters of credit, open aval-backed credit lines, provide bank guarantees, or supply a T2/TARGET2 direct settlement relationship; they are subject to frequent liquidity-raising limits and AML de-risking for electronics-wholesale business models; their ledger platforms are rarely ISO 20022 compliant for full supply-chain finance interoperability. Therefore, a fintech EMI is viable only as a second payment rail for Latin American receivables and USD disbursement optimization, while the primary corporate banking relationship must remain with a tier-1 Spanish bank able to offer the 'Credit_Line' target rail.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

UBO-déclaration opacity: non-resident shareholders, chain of corporate nominees, absence of natural-person identification above 25%.

Root cause: UBO-déclaration opacity: non-resident shareholders, chain of corporate nominees, absence of natural-person identification above 25%.

Defense evidence: Notarized Certificado de Titularidad Real issued by the Registro Mercantil; full multi-tier ownership charter up to the ultimate natural person or a listed-company exemption; apostilled passports and NIE/TIE of each ultimate beneficiary; a Board resolution confirming the 25% threshold test under Article 4.2 of Ley 10/2010; Spanish legal opinion confirming absence of nominee or fiduciary arrangements.
Dual-use and export-control red flags on multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC, HS 8532.24.00) and resistors (HS 8533.21.00), potentially classified as restricted strategic or military-grade goods.

Root cause: Dual-use and export-control red flags on multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCC, HS 8532.24.00) and resistors (HS 8533.21.00), potentially classified as restricted strategic or military-grade goods.

Defense evidence: EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 Annex-I self-assessment confirming commercial grade; component technical data sheets (X5R/X7R/C0G dielectric types, voltage ratings, package sizes) proving non-military specifications; ECCN classification from US origin exporters (EAR99); REACH/RoHS/EN 62368-1 certificates of conformity; end-user and end-use declarations from LatAm and EU buyers; signed non-embedded-weapons or non-military-end-use representation.
Grey-market and excess-inventory suspicion: invoice pricing materially below manufacturers' list price, high stock turnover, vague description of 'excess electronic inventory'.

Root cause: Grey-market and excess-inventory suspicion: invoice pricing materially below manufacturers' list price, high stock turnover, vague description of 'excess electronic inventory'.

Defense evidence: Complete provenance chain: original purchase invoices from franchised distributors or authorized EMS excess-stock programs; batch-level traceability registers (lot codes, date codes, OEM part numbers); Customs import SAD documents and TARIC codes; commercial correspondent contracts showing a 18-30% gross margin; ISO 9001:2015 quality certificate and inspection reports from third-party testing houses; insurance coverage for stored inventory; annual financial statements evidencing economic substance.
Payment-flow anomalies: rapid round-tripping to Latin America, unusual creditor jurisdictions, large cash-collateralized wires inconsistent with the low-risk electronics-wholesale profile.

Root cause: Payment-flow anomalies: rapid round-tripping to Latin America, unusual creditor jurisdictions, large cash-collateralized wires inconsistent with the low-risk electronics-wholesale profile.

Defense evidence: Approved customer/vendor KYC file for every counterparty; distribution agreements with 30-90 day payment terms; Pro-forma invoices and packing lists for each wire; SWIFT GPI end-to-end tracking; a 12-month rolling cash-flow forecast aligned with the inventory purchase pipeline; annual Form TE declaration to Banco de España demonstrating that all external transactions are statistically reported; a formal SEPBLAC-compliant internal AML manual and a designated compliance officer.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Equity contribution from the non-resident shareholder: the Spanish SL first opens a restricted capital escrow account ('Cuenta de Integración de Capital') at a tier-1 bank; the shareholder sends an MT103 SWIFT wire in EUR using the beneficiary IBAN and Field 70 purpose text 'Direct foreign investment — share capital subscription — ISIC 4652 / HS 8532.24.00 — wholesale of passive electronic components'; the bank issues a capital-disbursement certificate to the notary; the notary completes the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución) and files the D-1A investment-registration form with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores where the investment exceeds EUR 3,000,000 (smaller amounts are registered ex-post within 30 days); Banco de España statistical reporting applies through Form TE for any capital inflow >= EUR 50,000. Shareholder loan routing: execute a written intercompany loan agreement at arm's length, send MT103 with Field 70 'Shareholder loan — Article 16 LIS — non-resident direct lending — interest at market rate'; the Spanish bank requires the loan contract, the Form TE declaration and, where the lender is a connected party, a transfer-pricing benchmark. Verification requirements: bank confirms no shell-bank involvement, sanctions-screening of all ordering correspondents, and cash-flow consistency with the commercial activity described in the AML dossier. All EUR inbound non-SEPA flows arrive via TARGET2/SWIFT; euro-area intra-EU contributions use the SEPA Credit Transfer rail at no correspondent cost.For European and EUR-based supplier settlements: SEPA Credit Transfer or Instant SCT, plus the T2/TARGET2 high-value rail for amounts above EUR 100,000. For Asia-Pacific, LatAm and USD/CNY/JPY inventory purchases: SWIFT MT103 wire with a clearing correspondent bank; Field 70 must reference the underlying purchase order and invoice. Commercial letters of credit are issued as irrevocable LCs under UCP 600 via SWIFT MT700, with confirmation bank delivery in Japan, Korea, Taiwan or mainland China; negotiation and maturity payments are routed through MT754/MT400/MT910 reimbursement instructions. The 'Credit_Line' target rail is structured as a bilateral póliza de crédito (revolving working-capital facility) secured against MLCC/resistor inventory, covering up to 80% of approved purchase invoices, plus a documentary-import line supporting the issuance of LCs and standby LCs for inventory acquisition. For remittance to Latin American distributors, prefer MT103 with correspondent routing through US clearing banks or new-generation SWIFT Go to reduce fees; goods-export settlements must be reconciled with Form TE monthly filings. All disbursements must maintain a clear ISO 20022 structural reference: Unique End-to-End ID, instructed amount, beneficiary BIC+IBAN and correct purpose code (e.g., 'Trade in goods — electronic components' / 'Commercial credit — import/export financing').Spot FX — EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/JPY — executed at the treasury desk with DVP settlement inside T2/TARGET2 and CLS for eligible pairs.Outright FX Forwards (deliverable, tenor up to 12 months) under ISDA 2002 / FX Global Code, with CSA or credit-line collateralization; used to hedge USD/CNY payable and receivable windows.FX Swaps (swap de divisas) for rolling overnight liquidity between EUR and USD without disturbing the LC collateral block.Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-dated USD supplier financing versus EUR revenue streams.Non-Deliverable Forwards (EUR/CNH, USD/BRL, EUR/VND as applicable) under EMTA/ISDA 1998 NDF terms, solely for currencies with restricted onshore delivery; permissible as hedging only and requires EMIR NFC- status reporting.Vanilla European FX Options (call/put on EUR/USD or EUR/CNY) for costless-collared conversion of excess-electronics-inventory sale proceeds; subject to MiFID II appropriateness assessment.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Conditional — rated Low as a sole treasury spine and Medium as a supplementary settlement overlay. Spanish-licensed or passported EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) operating under PSD2 and supervised by Banco de España can open transactional EUR/GBP/USD accounts for an ES_SL without a physical branch visit, with e-KYC under RD 304/2014, and can provide cheaper MT103-correspondent-grade payments and FX conversion for the passive-components distribution flows. Legal constraints are material: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot issue commercial documentary letters of credit, open aval-backed credit lines, provide bank guarantees, or supply a T2/TARGET2 direct settlement relationship; they are subject to frequent liquidity-raising limits and AML de-risking for electronics-wholesale business models; their ledger platforms are rarely ISO 20022 compliant for full supply-chain finance interoperability. Therefore, a fintech EMI is viable only as a second payment rail for Latin American receivables and USD disbursement optimization, while the primary corporate banking relationship must remain with a tier-1 Spanish bank able to offer the 'Credit_Line' target rail.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general CIT (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014 (LIS); reduced 15% for newly created entities in the first two tax periods with a positive tax base (art. 29.3 LIS) subject to activity and legal-form requirements.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% under Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR, art. 25.1) generally. For EU/EEA recipient companies meeting the Parent-Subsidiary Directive conditions (5% or 10% holding? actually 5% under current law) and holding the shares for at least 12 months, the rate is 0% (exemption). For non-EU/EEA, treaty rates may reduce the 19% (e.g., 0% under certain DTAs with substantive holding thresholds).

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post-close date. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the due date is 25 July of the following year.

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Contabilidad del ejercico: 'Resultado contable' (Net accounting profit/loss before tax). Enter the company's statutory accounting profit per the audited annual accounts; for non-resident-owned SLs, reconcile with Spanish GAAP if foreign GAAP was used for external reporting. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 2 Diferencias permanentes - aumentos aplicados sobre el resultado contable (Permanent differences increasing the tax base). Report any non-deductible expenses (e.g., 5% dividend participation exemption, representation expenses over limits, donations). Non-resident shareholders should ensure arm's-length transfer pricing adjustments are not erroneously treated as permanent differences. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 3 Diferencias temporales - aumentos (Temporary differences increasing the tax base, e.g. depreciation with tax-effect). Include consolidation adjustments or accelerated depreciation; in an SL distribution business, focus on undue provisioning or inventory write-downs that require timing differences. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 4 Compensación de bases imponibles negativas de ejercicios anteriores (Loss carryforward offset). Apply available prior-year negative tax bases subject to the 70%/50% limit (see above) and the minimum EUR 1 million rule. Maintain traceable loss completion schedules. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 5 Base imponible (Net taxable base after all adjustments). This is the core line for tax computation. Non-resident parent companies must ensure transfer pricing documentation supports the resultant taxable base. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 6 Tipo de gravamen (Applicable CIT rate; 25% general, 15% if newly established). Select the correct code; for new SLs, verify the availability of the 15% rate and record the period of entitlement. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 7 Cuota íntegra (Gross tax liability). Calculated as taxable base times rate. No manual adjustment; system-computed. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 8 Deducciones, bonificaciones y pagos a cuenta (Credits, bonuses, and tax prepayments). Claim applicable R&D or double-taxation credits. Non-resident parents should reconcile any foreign tax credits (DTA relief) here for Brazil/LatAm operations as applicable. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 9 Retenciones y pagos fraccionados (Withholdings at source and installment tax payments). Report all Spanish source WHT suffered and quarterly installment payments made. Non-resident-owned SLs must coordinate WHT on interest/royalty payments with Form 193 annual returns. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.
Box 10 Resultado a ingresar / a devolver (Final tax due or refund). If refund claimed, verify bank account in Spain or foreign account with NIF; non-resident entities often use a Spanish tax representative for refund administration. Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge on the resulting tax due, increasing 1% for each full month of delay (max 20%). If no tax due, fixed penalty of EUR 200. Filing after official notice: 20% penalty. Delay beyond 12 months adds late-payment interest. Additionally, incorrect return due to neglect may incur penalty of 15% per art. 27 LGT.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Full Local File and Master File (Datos Maestros and Datos Locales) are required if the Spanish entity's net turnover is >= EUR 10 million (art. 18.3 LIS). Regardless of turnover, a contemporaneous record (simplified) must be maintained for all cross-border related-party transactions. Country-by-Country Reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue >= EUR 750 million.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not apply dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) similar to offshore jurisdictions, but the general anti-abuse rule (cláusula antielusión, art. 15 LIS) and substance-over-form doctrine (art. 13 LGT) allow the tax authorities to disregard artificial transactions lacking commercial justification. A 'shell company' with no employees, premises, or management in Spain may be reassessed as a foreign permanent establishment or a non-resident entity, denying treaty benefits and triggering 19% (or 24% for non-EU) WHT on deemed Spanish-source income. Substantiation of substance: lease agreement for a local office, payroll for at least 1–2 full-time staff, board minutes in Spain, and a genuine inventory-holding activity.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion (defraudación tributaria)

Statutory sanction: Penalty under General Tax Act (LGT) arts. 184-190: proportional sanction of 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, plus late-filing/or interest. Criminal offence under Criminal Code (CP) art. 305: if the defrauded quota exceeds EUR 120,000, imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of up to sextuple the defrauded amount.

Director personal liability: Directors can be held jointly and severally for civil debts (art. 42 LGT and 367 LSC). Criminal liability: personal imprisonment of directors who ordered or tolerated the evasion; travel bans and revocation of tax ID numbers possible during investigation.
Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure

Statutory sanction: AEAT may characterize the SL as a letterbox entity, denying CIT treaty benefits and levying a 15% (or 24%) withholding under IRNR on all invoiced amounts deemed distributed from Spain to the foreign parent. Additionally, an administrative penalty of EUR 1,500 to EUR 30,000 for obstruction of controls (art. 203 LGT) may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors who signed AEOI declarations or banking arrangements knowing the lack of substance may face civil joint liability for the tax shortfall (up to the company's unpaid tax) and possible criminal accomplice liability under art. 305 CP. In serious cases, the court may issue a temporary ban on leaving Spain.
Money Laundering / AML Deficiency (Law 10/2010)

Statutory sanction: SEPBLAC may impose fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 1,500,000 (serious infringement) or up to EUR 5,000,000 or 6 times the laundered value (very serious). Public reprimand and potential suspension of activity for 1–3 years can be added.

Director personal liability: Board members who knowingly allow third-party ownership structures without AML checks are personally liable for the fine (art. 58 Ley 10/2010) and may face imprisonment from 6 months to 3 years under art. 302 CP, plus a fine of up to triple the laundered assets and a travel-ban order.
Late Filing / Failure to File Form 200

Statutory sanction: Late filing without notification: 5% surcharge + 1% per month (max 20%) on tax due; if no tax due, EUR 200. If filed after official requirement, 20% penalty plus interest. Non-filing beyond 1 year: penalty of 20% and loss of ability to offset loss carryforwards; the tax debt becomes enforceable via attachment.

Director personal liability: Directors who caused the omission are jointly and severally liable for the penalty and interest (art. 42.2 LGT). In cases of criminal bankruptcy, a court may order a ban on managing similar companies for up to 10 years and abroad restrictions (travel ban).
